D24·a5yz — 2026-10-10
chose: 2.4 merge queue: landings run one at a time through a promise-chain queue in the driver. A branch that already contains the base fast-forwards as before, with no re-verify. A branch the base moved past is integrated in its own lane: rebased onto the base tip when it holds no merge commit, else (or when the rebase stops) merged with `git merge --no-edit`. Either way the gate runs again in the lane on the new tree, and a pass fast-forwards the base by compare-and-swap. A merge that stops on conflicts is LEFT IN PROGRESS in the lane: the task is reopened, the session's handoff is the new reason `merge_conflict` with the conflicting paths as its detail, and the lane's next session (the lane holds the branch, and its dirty tree keeps other tasks out) is told by the prompt, read from the lane's MERGE_HEAD and unmerged paths, to resolve, `git add` and `git commit`. A lane still holding unmerged paths at acceptance is never committed: that is a merge conflict again, with no gate. One task's merge_conflict handoffs in a run count against --max-verify-attempts and stop the run as stall when they reach it.
over: Rebase-only with the conflict aborted and the session told to `git rebase` (git rebase is outside the protocol floor, permissions.ts DEFAULT_ALLOW, so a driven session cannot run it, and a rebase in progress detaches HEAD so no lane would hold the branch); keeping the conflict in the record only (a resumed run's recover path has no session to file a handoff for, so the next prompt would lack it); stopping the run on any divergence (D20, D21's stop-until-2.4); rebasing at every launch.
because: Concurrent lanes make divergence the common case, so the D20 stop fired on most second landings. A merge left in the lane is finished with only `git add` and `git commit`, which the floor already grants, and its state is a fact git keeps, so the prompt is right on every path (runTask, recover, a resumed run). Rebasing first keeps the base linear for 2.6's bisect; merging a branch that already holds a merge keeps the session's resolution instead of replaying the conflict. A distinct handoff reason is what 2.5's merge-conflict reopen rate is counted from.
